Then during the Battle of the Camel, Ka'b ibn Sur al-Azdi, the judge (qadi) of Basra, who counted among the rebels, walked to the battlefield with a copy of the Quran and pleaded for the fighting to stop.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: It was consistently Mu'awiya's position that battle was the only option acceptable to the _____
Battle of Siffin.fact: It was consistently Mu'awiya's position that battle was the only option acceptable to the Syrians. The Syrians' call for arbitration thus indicates that Mu'awiya had sensed the potential of defeat, argue Madelung and McHugo.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: This tends to be the view of many other modern authors, some of whom add that Mu'awiya was advised to do so by Amr ibn al-As, citing al-Tabari and al-_____, among others
Battle of Siffin.fact: This tends to be the view of many other modern authors, some of whom add that Mu'awiya was advised to do so by Amr ibn al-As, citing al-Tabari and al-Baladhuri, among others.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: For his part, Ali is said to have exhorted his men to continue fighting, telling them to no avail that raising the _____ was for deception
Battle of Siffin.fact: Even so, Ali's army stopped fighting, perhaps because devout Muslims in his camp had been fighting to enforce the rule of the Quran all along, or simply because both armies were exhausted and a truce must have appealed to them, or because some in his camp saw the ceasefire as an opportunity to regain their influence over Ali. For his part, Ali is said to have exhorted his men to continue fighting, telling them to no avail that raising the Quran was for deception.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: The account of _____ too reflects this attitude of Ali
Battle of Siffin.fact: The account of Ibn Muzahim too reflects this attitude of Ali.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: In the former group, Mis'ar ibn _____ al-Tamimi and Zayd ibn Hisn al-Ta'i, who both later became Kharijite leaders, threatened to kill Ali if he did not answer the Syrians' call
Battle of Siffin.fact: In the former group, Mis'ar ibn Fadaki al-Tamimi and Zayd ibn Hisn al-Ta'i, who both later became Kharijite leaders, threatened to kill Ali if he did not answer the Syrians' call.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: The latter group included the ridda tribesmen of _____ and all newcomers to the city from their clans
Battle of Siffin.fact: The latter group included the ridda tribesmen of Kufa and all newcomers to the city from their clans.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: They followed al-Ash'ath ibn Qays, who told Ali that his clan would not fight for him if he refused the _____' call, as reported in Waq'at Siffin and Moruj
Battle of Siffin.fact: In the former group, Mis'ar ibn Fadaki al-Tamimi and Zayd ibn Hisn al-Ta'i, who both later became Kharijite leaders, threatened to kill Ali if he did not answer the Syrians' call. They followed al-Ash'ath ibn Qays, who told Ali that his clan would not fight for him if he refused the Syrians' call, as reported in Waq'at Siffin and Moruj.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Contrary to all these reports, an account by al-Kufi suggests that Ali welcomed the call to arbitration, even comparing it to the Treaty of _____ (628) by Muhammad
Battle of Siffin.fact: Contrary to all these reports, an account by al-Kufi suggests that Ali welcomed the call to arbitration, even comparing it to the Treaty of Hudaybiyya (628) by Muhammad.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Notwithstanding these two, modern authors tend to view Ali as opposed to the arbitration, including _____, McHugo, Poonawala, and Ayoub
Battle of Siffin.fact: Notwithstanding these two, modern authors tend to view Ali as opposed to the arbitration, including Madelung, McHugo, Poonawala, and Ayoub.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: The governor might have done so during his tenure under _____, and thus perhaps contemplated joining Mu'awiya in rebellion but was dissuaded from doing so
Battle of Siffin.fact: The governor might have done so during his tenure under Uthman, and thus perhaps contemplated joining Mu'awiya in rebellion but was dissuaded from doing so.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Ali later supported Hujr ibn Adi, a rival of al-Ash'ath within the Kinda tribe, and then removed the latter from his military post just before leaving Iraq, replacing him with Hasan ibn _____
Battle of Siffin.fact: Ali later supported Hujr ibn Adi, a rival of al-Ash'ath within the Kinda tribe, and then removed the latter from his military post just before leaving Iraq, replacing him with Hasan ibn Makhduj.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: These last two belonged to different _____ tribes and the appointment thus rekindled old tribal rivalries, according to Ayoub
Battle of Siffin.fact: These last two belonged to different Yemenite tribes and the appointment thus rekindled old tribal rivalries, according to Ayoub.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: While al-Ash'ath is also known to have expressed concern over the insecurity of Iran and the _____' threat during the civil war, Kennedy suggests that he also preferred a weakened Ali
Battle of Siffin.fact: While al-Ash'ath is also known to have expressed concern over the insecurity of Iran and the Byzantines' threat during the civil war, Kennedy suggests that he also preferred a weakened Ali.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: On the other hand, Mu'awiya's victory would have meant the subjugation and loss of _____ as the base of their power
Battle of Siffin.fact: On the other hand, Mu'awiya's victory would have meant the subjugation and loss of Iraq as the base of their power.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: The opinion of Hinds is close, while _____ similarly writes that the Kufan tribes had benefited from Uthman's policies and were not enthusiastic about the war with Mu'awiya
Battle of Siffin.fact: The opinion of Hinds is close, while Shaban similarly writes that the Kufan tribes had benefited from Uthman's policies and were not enthusiastic about the war with Mu'awiya.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: This is also the view of _____
Battle of Siffin.fact: This is also the view of Ayoub.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Perhaps they welcomed arbitration by the _____ because they had been fighting to enforce the rule of the Quran all along
Battle of Siffin.fact: Perhaps they welcomed arbitration by the Quran because they had been fighting to enforce the rule of the Quran all along.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Alternatively, _____ suggests that the qurra may have wanted a compromise with the Syrians that would have restricted the caliph
Battle of Siffin.fact: Alternatively, Kennedy suggests that the qurra may have wanted a compromise with the Syrians that would have restricted the caliph.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: His argument is that the Iraqi qurra had opposed _____ to gain more financial and political autonomy
Battle of Siffin.fact: His argument is that the Iraqi qurra had opposed Uthman to gain more financial and political autonomy. In contrast, Jafri first argues that the term qurra in early sources loosely refers to two groups: The first group was the Kufan qurra who revolted against Uthman and loyally supported Ali, led by the likes of Malik al-Ashtar and Hujr ibn Adi.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: They were thus willing to grant the same autonomy to the _____
Battle of Siffin.fact: Alternatively, Kennedy suggests that the qurra may have wanted a compromise with the Syrians that would have restricted the caliph. They were thus willing to grant the same autonomy to the Syrians.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: The second group was the _____ qurra and other tribesmen who conveniently advanced their claims under the cloak of Islamic priority
Battle of Siffin.fact: The second group was the Basran qurra and other tribesmen who conveniently advanced their claims under the cloak of Islamic priority. That the Kharijites consisted primarily of Basran tribesmen is also the view of the modern Islamicist Maria Dakake.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: It was at this point that the disillusioned second group rejected the arbitration and formed the _____
Battle of Siffin.fact: It was at this point that the disillusioned second group rejected the arbitration and formed the Kharijites. That the Kharijites consisted primarily of Basran tribesmen is also the view of the modern Islamicist Maria Dakake.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: That the _____ consisted primarily of Basran tribesmen is also the view of the modern Islamicist Maria Dakake
Battle of Siffin.fact: It was at this point that the disillusioned second group rejected the arbitration and formed the Kharijites. That the Kharijites consisted primarily of Basran tribesmen is also the view of the modern Islamicist Maria Dakake.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: He was silent at this point about revenge for _____ and removal of Ali from office
Battle of Siffin.fact: He was silent at this point about revenge for Uthman and removal of Ali from office.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: The proposal of Mu'awiya was accepted by the majority of Ali's army, reports al-_____
Battle of Siffin.fact: The proposal of Mu'awiya was accepted by the majority of Ali's army, reports al-Tabari.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: He declined it, however, saying that they would be crushed by the majority and the _____ who all demanded arbitration
Battle of Siffin.fact: He declined it, however, saying that they would be crushed by the majority and the Syrians who all demanded arbitration.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Some of these dissidents left for _____, while others stayed, perhaps hoping that Ali might later change his mind
Battle of Siffin.fact: Some of these dissidents left for Kufa, while others stayed, perhaps hoping that Ali might later change his mind. Later Ali defended his decision in Kufa, saying that he considered continuing the fight, alongside that minority, but feared that Hasan and Husayn would perish and with them the lineage of Muhammad.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Here, _____ criticizes Ali for this decision and suggests that he acted more like a tribal chief than the caliph
Battle of Siffin.fact: Here, Madelung criticizes Ali for this decision and suggests that he acted more like a tribal chief than the caliph.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Later Ali defended his decision in Kufa, saying that he considered continuing the fight, alongside that minority, but feared that Hasan and Husayn would perish and with them the lineage of _____
Battle of Siffin.fact: Later Ali defended his decision in Kufa, saying that he considered continuing the fight, alongside that minority, but feared that Hasan and Husayn would perish and with them the lineage of Muhammad.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Abu Musa was the former governor of Kufa, installed by the Iraqi rebels and later confirmed by Ali, who was dissuaded from removing him by al-_____
Battle of Siffin.fact: Abu Musa was the former governor of Kufa, installed by the Iraqi rebels and later confirmed by Ali, who was dissuaded from removing him by al-Ashtar.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Anyway, he was soon dismissed after opposing the war preparations for the Battle of the _____
Battle of Siffin.fact: Anyway, he was soon dismissed after opposing the war preparations for the Battle of the Camel.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Ali was also apparently concerned about _____'s political naivety, or about his neutrality
Battle of Siffin.fact: Abu Musa was the former governor of Kufa, installed by the Iraqi rebels and later confirmed by Ali, who was dissuaded from removing him by al-Ashtar. The majority in Ali's army also pressed for Abu Musa, even though he was reportedly neutral, and despite the opposition of Ali, who said he could not trust Abu Musa because he had earlier agitated against him.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: The alternatives proposed by Ali were _____ and al-Ashtar, according to Ibn Muzahim, both of whom were rejected by al-Ash'ath and other Yemenites, and also by the Iraqi qurra
Battle of Siffin.fact: The alternatives proposed by Ali were Ibn Abbas and al-Ashtar, according to Ibn Muzahim, both of whom were rejected by al-Ash'ath and other Yemenites, and also by the Iraqi qurra.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Mu'awiya was represented by his top general, Amr ibn al-As, who acted solely in the common interest of Mu'awiya and the _____
Battle of Siffin.fact: Mu'awiya was represented by his top general, Amr ibn al-As, who acted solely in the common interest of Mu'awiya and the Syrians.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: The two representatives committed to meet on neutral territory, to adhere to the _____ and Sunna and to save the community from war and division, a clause added evidently to appease the peace party
Battle of Siffin.fact: Veccia Vaglieri and Rahman write that the Iraqis were so convinced of the legitimacy of their cause that they insisted on the neutral Abu Musa, whereas others suggest that they were impressed by his piety, or his beautiful recitations of the Quran, or that he stood for provincial autonomy in Kufans' view. The two representatives committed to meet on neutral territory, to adhere to the Quran and Sunna and to save the community from war and division, a clause added evidently to appease the peac...

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Variations of this account are given by al-Tabari, _____, al-Kufi, and Ibn Abi'l-Hadid
Battle of Siffin.fact: Variations of this account are given by al-Tabari, Ibn Muzahim, al-Kufi, and Ibn Abi'l-Hadid.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: The two arbitrators were given a year to come to a decision, or until the end of _____, some seven months later, but this deadline was flexible
Battle of Siffin.fact: The two arbitrators were given a year to come to a decision, or until the end of Ramadan, some seven months later, but this deadline was flexible.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Bahramian puts their number at 12,000, citing al-_____ and al-Tabari
Battle of Siffin.fact: Bahramian puts their number at 12,000, citing al-Baladhuri and al-Tabari.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Ali visited them and told them that they had opted for the arbitration despite his warnings, according to al-_____
Battle of Siffin.fact: Bahramian puts their number at 12,000, citing al-Baladhuri and al-Tabari. Ali visited them and told them that they had opted for the arbitration despite his warnings, according to al-Tabari.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: But when the seceders returned to _____, they accused Ali of having nullified the arbitration agreement, which he denied, saying that he was committed to the formal agreement with Mu'awiya
Battle of Siffin.fact: But when the seceders returned to Kufa, they accused Ali of having nullified the arbitration agreement, which he denied, saying that he was committed to the formal agreement with Mu'awiya.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Similar statements are attributed to Ali by _____ and Ibn Abi'l-Hadid, in which the caliph vows to uphold the covenant with Mu'awiya
Battle of Siffin.fact: Similar statements are attributed to Ali by Ibn Muzahim and Ibn Abi'l-Hadid, in which the caliph vows to uphold the covenant with Mu'awiya.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: In another account by al-_____, Ali cites verse 16:91 for upholding the treaty when two Kharijites, namely, Zur'a ibn al-Burj al-Ta'i and Hurqus ibn Zuhayr al-Sa'di, appealed to him to revoke it
Battle of Siffin.fact: In another account by al-Tabari, Ali cites verse 16:91 for upholding the treaty when two Kharijites, namely, Zur'a ibn al-Burj al-Ta'i and Hurqus ibn Zuhayr al-Sa'di, appealed to him to revoke it.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Many of the dissidents apparently accepted Ali's position, while the rest left for al-_____, a town near al-Mada'in, and there declared Abd Allah ibn Wahb al-Rasibi (d
Battle of Siffin.fact: Many of the dissidents apparently accepted Ali's position, while the rest left for al-Nahrawan, a town near al-Mada'in, and there declared Abd Allah ibn Wahb al-Rasibi (d. ' seceders'), who later took up arms against Ali in the Battle of Nahrawan (658).

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: ' seceders'), who later took up arms against Ali in the Battle of _____ (658)
Battle of Siffin.fact: Many of the dissidents apparently accepted Ali's position, while the rest left for al-Nahrawan, a town near al-Mada'in, and there declared Abd Allah ibn Wahb al-Rasibi (d. ' seceders'), who later took up arms against Ali in the Battle of Nahrawan (658).

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: They soon labeled anyone who opposed them as nonbelievers, who had to be fought, thus becoming the forerunners of _____ terrorism, according to some
Battle of Siffin.fact: They soon labeled anyone who opposed them as nonbelievers, who had to be fought, thus becoming the forerunners of Islamic terrorism, according to some.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: After being silent about it initially, the _____ now said that they also wanted the arbitrators to judge whether the killing of Uthman was justified, about which the qurra had no doubts
Battle of Siffin.fact: After being silent about it initially, the Syrians now said that they also wanted the arbitrators to judge whether the killing of Uthman was justified, about which the qurra had no doubts.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Hinds and _____ thus regard the arbitration as a skillfully-planned maneuver to disintegrate the coalition of Ali
Battle of Siffin.fact: Alternatively, Hinds and Poonawala believe that the seceders were disillusioned with the arbitration process, particularly by the removal of Ali's title of amir al-mu'minin in the final agreement and by its reference to the Sunna next to the Quran, as noted also in Waq'at Siffin. Hinds and Poonawala thus regard the arbitration as a skillfully-planned maneuver to disintegrate the coalition of Ali.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: For Ayoub, the seceders were frustrated with a costly war that had achieved nothing and denounced the agreement that questioned the authority of the legitimate _____ caliph, in their view
Battle of Siffin.fact: For Ayoub, the seceders were frustrated with a costly war that had achieved nothing and denounced the agreement that questioned the authority of the legitimate Muslim caliph, in their view.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: This is the understanding of _____, Veccia Vaglieri, Caetani, and Bahramian, while some others believe that the two arbitrators met only once
Battle of Siffin.fact: This is the understanding of Madelung, Veccia Vaglieri, Caetani, and Bahramian, while some others believe that the two arbitrators met only once. As an early companion of Muhammad, it is similarly the understanding of Madelung that Abu Musa did not support the caliphate of Mu'awiya, a taliq.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: The account of al-_____ depicts Abu Musa as opposed to the caliphates of both Ali and Mu'awiya
Battle of Siffin.fact: The account of al-Tabari depicts Abu Musa as opposed to the caliphates of both Ali and Mu'awiya.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: As an early companion of _____, it is similarly the understanding of Madelung that Abu Musa did not support the caliphate of Mu'awiya, a taliq
Battle of Siffin.fact: As an early companion of Muhammad, it is similarly the understanding of Madelung that Abu Musa did not support the caliphate of Mu'awiya, a taliq.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Ideally, however, _____ may have preferred a broad shura that included Ali and Abd Allah ibn Umar
Battle of Siffin.fact: The account of al-Tabari depicts Abu Musa as opposed to the caliphates of both Ali and Mu'awiya. As an early companion of Muhammad, it is similarly the understanding of Madelung that Abu Musa did not support the caliphate of Mu'awiya, a taliq.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: The similar account of _____ is that Abu Musa proposed removing Ali and installing the neutral Abd Allah ibn Umar for the caliphate, even though Abd Allah was probably uninterested in it
Battle of Siffin.fact: The similar account of Ibn Muzahim is that Abu Musa proposed removing Ali and installing the neutral Abd Allah ibn Umar for the caliphate, even though Abd Allah was probably uninterested in it.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: This attitude of _____ is also evident in an account given by al-Kufi and al-Tabari, who write that Mu'awiya sent al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba to assess the arbitrators' progress
Battle of Siffin.fact: Ideally, however, Abu Musa may have preferred a broad shura that included Ali and Abd Allah ibn Umar. The similar account of Ibn Muzahim is that Abu Musa proposed removing Ali and installing the neutral Abd Allah ibn Umar for the caliphate, even though Abd Allah was probably uninterested in it.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Perhaps as an opener for the peace negotiations, the two arbitrators first discussed the assassination of _____, most likely at the initiative of Amr
Battle of Siffin.fact: Perhaps as an opener for the peace negotiations, the two arbitrators first discussed the assassination of Uthman, most likely at the initiative of Amr. They reached the verdict that Uthman had been killed wrongfully and that Mu'awiya had the right to seek revenge, but could not agree on anything else, either because Amr blocked the choice of Ali for the caliphate or a fresh shura, or because Abu Musa was adamant in his opposition to Mu'awiya.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Madelung views the verdict about Uthman as a political one, a judicial misjudgment, and a blunder of the naive _____, who might have hoped that Amr would later reciprocate his concession
Battle of Siffin.fact: Abu Musa answered that they were the best of mankind for they did not carry its burden, while Amr answered that they were the worst of mankind for neither they upheld a truth nor repudiated a falsehood. They reached the verdict that Uthman had been killed wrongfully and that Mu'awiya had the right to seek revenge, but could not agree on anything else, either because Amr blocked the choice of Ali for the caliphate or a fresh shura, or because Abu Musa was adamant in his opposition to Mu'awiya.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: In particular, Ali denounced the conduct of the two arbitrators as contrary to the _____ and began preparations for a second expedition to Syria
Battle of Siffin.fact: In particular, Ali denounced the conduct of the two arbitrators as contrary to the Quran and began preparations for a second expedition to Syria.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Some of these were from Hejaz and had remained neutral throughout the conflict, perhaps lured to _____ by the promise of a broad shura for choosing the next caliph
Battle of Siffin.fact: Some of these were from Hejaz and had remained neutral throughout the conflict, perhaps lured to Udhruh by the promise of a broad shura for choosing the next caliph.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Their presence was nevertheless a major coup, suggests _____, because Hejaz was still controlled by Ali at the time
Battle of Siffin.fact: Their presence was nevertheless a major coup, suggests Madelung, because Hejaz was still controlled by Ali at the time.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: In particular, that _____ ibn Umar accepted the invitation of Mu'awiya hints at his interest in the caliphate, contrary to the rumors showing him uninterested
Battle of Siffin.fact: Not part of the arbitration process, this second meeting was solely an initiative of Mu'awiya, who also invited the sons of prominent companions to take part, including Abd Allah ibn Umar, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, and some others. In particular, that Abd Allah ibn Umar accepted the invitation of Mu'awiya hints at his interest in the caliphate, contrary to the rumors showing him uninterested.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: As for the final scene of the Udhruh meeting, one popular account is that _____ deposed both Ali and Mu'awiya and called for a council to appoint the new caliph per his earlier agreement with Amr
Battle of Siffin.fact: The negotiations failed eventually, as the two arbitrators could not agree on the next caliph: Amr supported Mu'awiya, while Abu Musa nominated his son-in-law Abd Allah ibn Umar, who stood down in the interest of unity by his own account, or because he was intimidated by Mu'awiya, who is said to have threatened him in the closing gala. As for the final scene of the Udhruh meeting, one popular account is that Abu Musa deposed both Ali and Mu'awiya and called for a council to appoint the new ca...

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: When Amr took the stage, however, he deposed Ali but confirmed Mu'awiya as the governor of Syria, thus breaking his agreement with _____
Battle of Siffin.fact: The negotiations failed eventually, as the two arbitrators could not agree on the next caliph: Amr supported Mu'awiya, while Abu Musa nominated his son-in-law Abd Allah ibn Umar, who stood down in the interest of unity by his own account, or because he was intimidated by Mu'awiya, who is said to have threatened him in the closing gala. As for the final scene of the Udhruh meeting, one popular account is that Abu Musa deposed both Ali and Mu'awiya and called for a council to appoint the new ca...

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: Similar variants of this account are recounted by _____ and al-Kufi
Battle of Siffin.fact: Similar variants of this account are recounted by Ibn Muzahim and al-Kufi.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: The Kufan delegation then reacted furiously to _____'s concessions, and he fled to Mecca in disgrace, whereas Amr was well-received by Mu'awiya upon his return to Syria
Battle of Siffin.fact: As for the final scene of the Udhruh meeting, one popular account is that Abu Musa deposed both Ali and Mu'awiya and called for a council to appoint the new caliph per his earlier agreement with Amr. When Amr took the stage, however, he deposed Ali but confirmed Mu'awiya as the governor of Syria, thus breaking his agreement with Abu Musa.
